pairs.subject: eval-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/responder/src/investigate.rs:82 When judge scores drop, the investigation prompt sends the investigator only to system-side owners (prompt, model or parameters, retrieval, code). It never lists the upstream owners failure-attribution requires checking first — the label, the dataset or scored-traffic mix, the input construction — or the instrument itself, so a dataset, label or judge change gets diagnosed as a product defect.

techniques.evidence: crates/responder/src/investigate.rs:82 The owner list leaves out label, dataset and input layers (most upstream first) and the judge, and the investigation works on one alert at a time instead of classes.

crates/responder/src/classify.rs:14 Classification here is operational triage (transient vs code), not a benchmark pass rate; the fallback detector does count its own use, which is in the spirit of the technique.

pairs.subject: eval-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/mcp/src/prompts.rs:105 The benchmark-leaderboard MCP prompt tells the agent to call a regression by comparing the latest run's mean with the prior run's — one sample each, with no interval. It does not route through the regression/gate tools the server already exposes (check_benchmark_gate, get_benchmark_regression), so a second sample gets read as a correction or regression.

techniques.evidence: crates/mcp/src/prompts.rs:105 Run-vs-prior on point means: a re-run at the same n is a second sample, not evidence of regression.
crates/mcp/src/schemas.rs:186 Judge trust comes from calibration and is three-valued; calibrations carry agreement plus n.

pairs.subject: eval-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/store-pg/src/score_summary.rs:65 The Postgres score summary groups only by the event dimension and filters optionally by rubric_id. It never filters or groups by scored_by (the judge model), so verdicts from different judges, and from different rubric versions when rubric_id is omitted, are pooled into one mean and one CI — splicing different instruments into one series.

techniques.evidence: crates/store-pg/src/score_summary.rs:65 Each score carries scored_by and rubric_id, but the summary aggregates across judges; the standard says scores from different judge packets must not be spliced.
crates/store-pg/src/dataset_lineage.rs:136 Frozen datasets refuse edits; a fork mints the next version past the highest version the name carries (line 46), so scenario sets are versioned fixtures.
crates/store-pg/src/calibrations.rs:3 A re-calibration adds a row instead of overwriting the earlier measurement, so disagreeing measurements stay visible side by side.
